description:
This role is for one of our clients 
 Compensation: $70 - $90 per hour 
 
 Role Type: Independent Contractor
 Work Arrangement: Fully Remote
 Schedule: Flexible – Work on your own schedule
 Payment Frequency: Weekly via Stripe or Wise
 About the Role
 We are seeking an experienced GPU Kernel Engineer – AI Expert to evaluate the quality, correctness, and completeness of GPU and accelerator kernel development tasks used to train and assess advanced AI models.
 In this role, you will review kernel development tasks across multiple frameworks and hardware platforms, focusing on numerical accuracy, performance-benchmarking fairness, task specifications, and compilation and runtime reliability. You will assess whether implementations meet technical requirements, identify potential issues, and provide clear, structured, rubric-based feedback to improve the quality of AI-generated kernel solutions.
 The ideal candidate has hands-on experience developing, optimizing, or verifying kernels across multiple GPU and accelerator ecosystems, including CUDA, Triton, NKI, or Pallas.
 Requirements 
 Key Responsibilities
 Evaluate GPU and accelerator kernel development tasks for technical quality, correctness, completeness, and implementation feasibility.
 Assess numerical correctness using appropriate absolute, relative, and ULP-based tolerances, along with reliable reference implementations.
 Review performance benchmarks for fairness, consistency, and reproducibility across hardware and software environments.
 Evaluate task specifications for clarity, completeness, appropriate scope, and technical accuracy.
 Identify compilation and runtime issues, including driver incompatibilities, out-of-memory errors, launch-configuration problems, shape and stride mismatches, and autotuning failures.
 Assess kernel generation, framework translation, hardware migration, debugging, performance optimization, and operator-fusion tasks.
 Analyze performance bottlenecks using profiling tools, roofline analysis, and framework-native performance utilities.
 Provide actionable, rubric-based written feedback to improve kernel implementations and evaluation standards.
 Basic Qualifications
 3+ years of hands-on experience developing, optimizing, or verifying GPU and accelerator kernels using at least two of the following: CUDA, Triton, NKI, or Pallas (JAX) .
 Strong understanding of kernel numerical-correctness criteria, including absolute and relative tolerances, ULP-based comparisons, and reference-implementation selection.
 Demonstrated experience with performance profiling and benchmarking using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight, Nsight Compute (NCU), roofline analysis, or framework-native profilers.
 Familiarity with common compilation and runtime failure modes, including driver mismatches, out-of-memory errors, launch-configuration issues, shape/stride mismatches, and autotuning failures.
 Experience with at least three kernel development task types, such as:
 Kernel generation from technical specifications.
 Translation or lowering across frameworks.
 Migration between hardware targets.
 Kernel debugging and verification.
 Performance optimization.
 Operator fusion.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working across both NVIDIA GPU ecosystems (CUDA/Triton) and custom accelerator platforms (NKI/Pallas/TPU).
 Background in compiler engineering, MLIR, or intermediate-representation lowering.
 Strong understanding of memory-hierarchy optimization, including shared-memory tiling, register pressure, bank conflicts, and memory-coalescing patterns.
 Contributions to kernel libraries or related open-source projects, such as cuBLAS, cuDNN, Triton community kernels, or JAX/XLA custom calls.
 Contract and Payment Terms
 Engagement as an independent contractor.
 Fully remote role with a flexible schedule.
 Projects may be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on project requirements and performance.
 Work will not require access to confidential or proprietary information belonging to any current or former employer, client, or institution.
 Payments are made weekly through Stripe or Wise, based on services rendered.
 H-1B and STEM OPT candidates cannot be supported at this time.
